title: Kiteworks is a private-cloud file-sharing/governance appliance with web app, email protection gateway, and API
detail: Kiteworks' own documentation describes the platform as a hardened virtual appliance (private cloud / on-prem / hybrid / FedRAMP deployments) that unifies secure file sharing, email (with Email Protection Gateway, EPG), managed file transfer, web forms, and REST APIs under centralized governance/compliance controls.
evidence: kiteworks.com: 'Kiteworks secure email ... including the Email Protection Gateway that automates email protection'; 'Automate and secure large-scale file transfer operations with a hardened virtual appliance'; 'Build Integrations, Applications, and Automated Management Using a Powerful REST API'; 'Add secure, governed file transfer and email to mobile apps, web apps, forms'; hardened virtual appliance with embedded firewall and WAF; deployment options include on-premise, private cloud, hybrid and FedRAMP.

title: Kiteworks program scope and exclusions verification
detail: From the live YesWeHack program page: scope explicitly includes the Kiteworks Core node (listed first in 'Kiteworks ecosystem', described as the operation of a single Kiteworks Core node on a hardened appliance; 'For Kiteworks Core, which holds our crown jewels' with a $25k bonus bounty). Exclusions verified in Program Rules/Eligibility: DoS forbidden ('Attempting any type of Denial of Service attacks'); automated tools explicitly called out ('refrain from using automated tools, and limit yourself about requests per second'); user-data access/manipulation excluded ('You must not leak, manipulate, or destroy any user data'); destructive validation excluded ('Deleting other user accounts', 'Decommissioning any boxes', interference with infrastructure). Claim CONFIRMED on all components.
evidence: Live page text L91 (Core Node scope), L105 (KW Access asset), L116-119 ($25k bonus for unauth RCE as root on Kiteworks Core), L34 (DoS forbidden), L75-76 (refrain from automated tools + rate limit), L78 (no leak/manipulate/destroy user data), L40/L48 (no decommissioning, no deleting other user accounts).

title: Claim: Kiteworks has publicly known CVEs; v9.5.1 addressed all known vulns (Sept 2026)
detail: Both halves confirmed from public sources. Kiteworks' own Sept 25, 2026 advisory states: 'Kiteworks has accounted for all known vulnerabilities in our current release, 9.5.1' (CISO Frank Balonis quote, kiteworks.com press release). Public CVEs include: CVE-2026-29092 (Email Protection Gateway session, 4.9), CVE-2026-23514 (Core access control, 8.8), CVE-2026-24750 (Secure Data Forms, 7.6), CVE-2025-53939 (Core improper input validation, 6.3), CVE-2025-53900/53899/53897/53896 (MFT, 6.5-7.2), CVE-2023-7273 (ownCloud CSRF), CVE-2024-28063/28064 (Totemomail, incl. 9.8 critical), CVE-2021-31586/31585 (SQLi, privilege escalation), CVE-2016-5662/5663/5664 (appliance). Notable: none of the Core CVEs found carry CVSS 10.0, and no evidence of a specific 9.5.1 CVE fix list was found — only the company's general 'accounted for all known vulnerabilities' statement.
evidence: https://www.kiteworks.com/company/press-releases/kiteworks-precautionary-shutdown-advisory/ (Sept 25, 2026) | https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/25/kiteworks-urges-customers-to-shut-down-their-servers-amid-imminent-threat-of-cyberattack/ | http://thehackernews.com/2026/09/kiteworks-urges-customers-to-shut-down.html | OpenCVE listings: CVE-2026-29092, CVE-2026-23514, CVE-2026-24750, CVE-2025-53939, CVE-2025-53900, CVE-2025-53899, CVE-2025-53897, CVE-2025-53896, CVE-2023-7273, CVE-2024-28063, CVE-2024-28064, CVE-2021-31586, CVE-2021-31585

title: Kiteworks $25k Crown Jewels bonus for unauthenticated RCE as root on Core
detail: Claim fully matches the live program page reward guidelines: $25,000 bonus on top of the HIGH asset reward grid for a new, previously unreported unauthenticated (CVSS PR:N) RCE as root on the Kiteworks Core appliance; the CRITICAL finding reward grid lists $50,000 at CVSS 10.0.
evidence: L116-119: "For Kiteworks Core, which holds our crown jewels, we offer a $25,000 bonus bounty (on top of the asset reward grid HIGH) for a very specific scenario: If you report a new, previously unreported vulnerability (or a chain of new vulnerabilities) that allows an unauthenticated attacker (CVSS PR:N) to achieve remote code execution (RCE) as root on the Kiteworks Core appliance, you qualify for this bonus." L131-135 reward grid header "CVSS Score | Bounty (HIGH reward grid + 25,000 Bonus)" with 10.0 = $50,000. Caveat from page: root must be on the underlying hardened appliance itself, not a single container.

title: Kiteworks public REST API documented for files, folders, shares, users, workflows
detail: Kiteworks publishes a public REST API via its developer portal at developer.kiteworks.com (400+ endpoints, OAuth 2.0). Documented categories: Content APIs (/users, /folders, /files with upload/download/copy/move/delete/versioning/sharing, /sources); Collaboration APIs (/mail, comments nested under /files, /tasks — explicitly described as orchestrating 'collaborative workflows'); Contacts APIs (/contacts, /groups, /ldapGroups); Security APIs (/profiles, /roles, /adminRoles, /devices, /admin including /admin/users); Client Management (/clients, /scopes); Maintenance (/licenses). All five claimed areas (files, folders, shares, users, workflows) are covered; sharing lives under /files and workflow orchestration under Collaboration APIs, not under dedicated /shares or /workflows paths.
evidence: developer.kiteworks.com API Endpoints page: 'The Kiteworks API covers the full breadth of the platform, organised into seven categories.' Content APIs cover /users, /folders, /files; file endpoints cover 'upload and download, copy, move and delete, lock and unlock, versioning, and file sharing'; Collaboration APIs expose 'mail, comments, and tasks' to 'participate in or orchestrate collaborative workflows'; /admin/users covers 'list, add, update, and delete users'. Portal home: '400+ API Endpoints', 'OAuth 2.0 Auth Standard'.

title: Kiteworks excluded/accepted-risk classes confirmed from live policy
detail: All six claimed classes appear in the live YesWeHack Kiteworks policy: non-qualifying list excludes user enumeration, race condition, rate-limit/bypass issues, self-XSS, and best-practice flaws without PoC; Known Issues/Accepted risks lists AV/filetype bypass by renaming and internal user-ID listing.
evidence: Non-qualifying (program page L423/L425/L454/L456/L484): Self-XSS or XSS that cannot be used to impact other users; Any hypothetical flaw or best practices without exploitable vulnerabilities and PoC; Lack or bypass of rate-limiting, brute-forcing or captcha issues; User enumeration (e.g. email, alias, GUID, phone number, common CMS endpoints); Race condition. Known Issues/Accepted risks (L254/L256): Bypassing AV or filetype restrictions (by renaming files or changing content type, etc.); Listing internal users by ID.

detail: Read the full live YesWeHack Kiteworks Public Bug Bounty program page. The 'Instances description / Kiteworks Access' section names exactly one access URL: https://ywh-kw-public.bounty.kiteworks.dev. title: Kiteworks AV scanning and DLP policy evaluation claim
detail: Claim: 'Kiteworks processes uploaded files through antivirus scanning and DLP (data loss prevention) policy evaluation.' Independently verified against Kiteworks' own public documentation. AV CONFIRMED: Kiteworks Security Architecture white paper states 'Kiteworks uses F-Secure Atlant antivirus to check incoming and outgoing files.' DLP + policy evaluation CONFIRMED: the same white paper describes a 'flexible policybased system that offers granular access and sharing controls' where 'The system uses the DLP scan results to classify every version of every file' (Scanned: OK / Scanned: Blocked / Unscanned) and 'enforces different access and sharing restrictions for each data classification.' Kiteworks' Advanced Governance page states DLP identifies 'PII, PHI, IP, or other sensitive information in outgoing files' and files can be set to 'block sending of failing files,' plus its GDPR Compliance Report section shows 'which files have passed or failed AV, DLP, and ATP scans.' Caveat: AV white paper is the 2023 edition; marketing DLP text focuses on outbound transfers, but the white paper explicitly ties DLP scan results to policy evaluation on every file version. No original reasoning was consulted.
evidence: 1) Kiteworks Security Architecture white paper (kiteworks.com, 2023): 'Kiteworks uses F-Secure Atlant antivirus to check incoming and outgoing files.' 2) Same white paper: 'Kiteworks has developed a flexible policybased system that offers granular access and sharing controls... The system uses the DLP scan results to classify every version of every file... Scanned: OK. Files that were scanned by a DLP system and passed OK. Scanned: Blocked. Files that were scanned by a DLP system and were found to contain sensitive data. Unscanned: Files that have not yet been scanned... Kiteworks then enforces different access and sharing restrictions for each data classification.' 3) kiteworks.com/platform/advanced-governance/: 'DLP Content Scanning, Blocking, and Visibility — Protect your outgoing data from inadvertent or intentional leaks, using your best-in-class DLP solution to identify PII, PHI, IP, or other sensitive information in outgoing files... Or you can set it to block sending of failing files.' 4) Same page: GDPR Compliance Report 'show which files have passed or failed AV, DLP, and ATP scans.'

title: Verify: Kiteworks supports LDAP/AD integration and SSO (SAML)
detail: CLAIM CONFIRMED from Kiteworks public documentation. (1) Kiteworks Statement of Work - Integration v1.0.2 (kiteworks.com, Copyright 2019-2022 Kiteworks, Inc.): Core System building block lists: Connect one or more directory service (AD, LDAP) to the Kiteworks core system for internal users, define user profiles. Define the accepted authentication methods and connect to the customers SSO/MFA system(s). Same doc, Authentication & authorization configuration row: LDAP, SSO, 2FA, profile definition & mapping. (2) Kiteworks Getting Started Guide v8.2.0-01 (October 2023, Copyright 2023 Kiteworks): Tip: When LDAP or single signon policies are in place for your company, you typically enter a user name instead of an email address. (3) SAML protocol corroboration: Microsoft official Entra ID tutorial Configure Kiteworks for Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID (learn.microsoft.com) walks through Set up Single Sign-On with SAML for the Kiteworks enterprise app with Entity ID https://<kiteworksURL>/sp/module.php/saml/sp/saml2-acs.php/sp-sso. Independent verifier never saw original reasoning; conclusion drawn solely from quoted docs.
evidence: Q1: https://www.kiteworks.com/sites/default/files/resources/sp/Statement%20of%20Work%20-%20Kiteworks%20Integration.pdf -> Connect one or more directory service (AD, LDAP) to the Kiteworks core system for internal users... connect to the customers SSO/MFA system(s) | Authentication & authorization configuration: LDAP, SSO, 2FA, profile definition & mapping. Q2: https://global.mftservice.com/sw/guide/Kiteworks_Getting_Started_Guide.pdf -> Tip: When LDAP or single signon policies are in place for your company, you typically enter a user name instead of an email address. Q3: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/saas-apps/kiteworks-tutorial -> On the Select a Single sign-on method page, select SAML... Identifier (Entity ID): https://<kiteworksURL>/sp/module.php/saml/sp/saml2-acs.php/sp-sso
